prompt.context: Big Beer Co is a multinational drink and brewing company with $50 billion in annual sales. Big Beer Co is the industry leader in terms of market share and boasts a portfolio of hundreds of different beer brands. It has seen consistent growth over time, with recent growth stemming from acquisitions of craft beer breweries and mergers with other multinationals. Wary of ever-changing consumer tastes and the need to deliver value to shareholders, the board is concerned about the go-forward viability of the current corporate strategy. Recently, non-alcoholic alternatives, hard kombucha, and alcoholic seltzer have grown in popularity as Millennials and Gen Z come of age, with alcoholic seltzer being the most attractive option.
prompt.question: The CEO has brought you in to determine the following: should Big Beer Co enter the alcoholic seltzer market? And how should it enter the market?

clarifying_info.a: Big Beer Co will only launch in the US market.

clarifying_info.q: What is the financial target or hurdle rate?
clarifying_info.a: The board is looking for initiatives that increase margins by $500M by year 5. Big Beer Co expects investments to have a payback period of 5 years or less. There is no discount rate to factor in.

clarifying_info.q: Does Big Beer Co manufacture in-house or outsource?
clarifying_info.a: Big Beer Co manufactures in-house and distributes through third parties.
Manufacturing capacity is not currently a constraint.

exhibits.title: Annual Alcoholic Seltzer Sales (in USD)
exhibits.shows: A table listing four competitors in the alcoholic seltzer market with their market share and 2020 sales figures. One competitor's 2020 sales figure is given; the others are marked with question marks. A note states that alcoholic seltzer sales are set to double in 5 years.

data.note: Alcoholic Seltzer sales are set to double in 5 years

exhibits.title: Market Entry Options
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of three market entry modes — Internal Launch, Joint Venture, and Acquisition — across four dimensions: Annual Revenue, Operating Expenditures (as % of revenue), Up-front Costs, and Time-to-Market.

framework: 1. Alcoholic Seltzer Market: (a) Size — current size, growth/decline trajectory, trends; (b) Competitors — positioning, relative market share; (c) Consumers — segments, preferences, purchase drivers
2. Financial: (a) Revenue — volume, average selling price (ASP); (b) Costs — variable costs (sales commissions, transportation, raw materials, labor), fixed costs (PP&E, rent, marketing, R&D, SG&A)
3. Risks: brand risk, regulatory risk, opportunity costs, consumer education, changing consumer tastes, macroeconomic conditions, cannibalization

questions.prompt: How big will the alcoholic seltzer market be in five years?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 1 to first calculate 2020 total market size from Competitor 2's known share and sales, then apply the stated doubling rule. Strong candidates compute all four competitors' 2020 sales as a cross-check.

math.setup: Competitor 2 has 25% market share and $500M in 2020 sales. Total 2020 market = $500M / 0.25 = $2 billion. Alcoholic seltzer sales double in 5 years, so 5-year market = $2B x 2 = $4 billion. Verify by computing other competitors: total units proxy = 500 x 4 = 2000 units index. Competitor 1 (60%): (500x4) x 0.1 x 6 = $1.2B; Competitor 3 (10%): (500x4) x 0.1 = $200M; Competitor 4 (5%): (500x4) x 0.1 x 0.5 = $100M. Sum: $1,200M + $500M + $200M + $100M = $2,000M = $2B (confirms 2020 market size).
steps: Cross-check Competitor 1 (60%): $4B x 60% = $2.4B in year 5 (or $1.2B today)
Cross-check Competitor 3 (10%): $4B x 10% = $400M in year 5 (or $200M today)
Cross-check Competitor 4 (5%): $4B x 5% = $200M in year 5 (or $100M today)
math.answer: The alcoholic seltzer market will be $4 billion in five years.

questions.prompt: What are some ways that Big Beer Co could enter the alcoholic seltzer market? Which entry mode is best based on the financial data?
questions.guidance: Candidate should first volunteer the three entry modes (internal/organic launch, joint venture, acquisition) before seeing Exhibit 2. After Exhibit 2 is shown, candidate calculates annual contribution margin and 5-year NPV for each option and identifies that all three satisfy the payback requirement but the Internal Launch has the highest NPV.

math.setup: Annual Contribution Margin = Annual Revenue x (1 - Operating Expenditure %). 5-year NPV = (Annual Contribution Margin x payback years) - Up-front Costs. Payback years for each option are constrained by 5-year horizon and time-to-market: Internal Launch starts generating returns after 24 months (year 3 onward = 3 full years); Joint Venture starts after 12 months (4 years); Acquisition starts immediately (5 years).
steps: All three exceed $500M margin target by year 5; Internal Launch has highest NPV at $1.75B
math.answer: Internal Launch NPV $1.75B > Joint Venture NPV $1.5B > Acquisition NPV $1.0B. Recommend Internal Launch.

questions.prompt: What are some considerations that should be included in Big Beer Co's go-to-market plan?
questions.guidance: Candidate should be structured, MECE, and creative. A strong answer covers: Who (target segments — millennials, Gen Z), What (product form factor: size, alcohol content, caloric content, flavors), and How (social media promotion, brand positioning for younger generations, celebrity endorsements, prominent placement in channels frequented by younger demographics).

questions.prompt: (Optional) In addition to moving into the alcoholic seltzer market, the CEO has asked you to enumerate other potential initiatives for Big Beer Co. What else could the company do to increase profitability?
questions.guidance: Candidate should be structured, MECE, and creative. Strong answers include: (1) Enter other product categories (wine, spirits, non-alcoholic beverages, food); (2) Refresh advertising strategy (influencer marketing, TikTok); (3) Target new segments or geographies (developing economies); (4) Divest lagging parts of the business (sell poor-performing brands or exit poor-performing regions); (5) Vertical integration or disintegration (spin off manufacturing or move into agricultural production or distribution).

brainstorming.prompt: What are some considerations that should be included in Big Beer Co's go-to-market plan for entering the alcoholic seltzer market?

categories.name: Who (Target Segments)
ideas: Gen Z consumers coming of age
Health-conscious drinkers looking for lighter options

categories.name: What (Product Design)
ideas: Variety of fruit flavors to match competitor offerings

categories.name: How (Go-to-Market Execution)
ideas: Social media campaigns (Instagram, TikTok, influencer partnerships)
Celebrity endorsements to build brand credibility with younger demos
Prominent shelf placement in channels frequented by target demographics (convenience stores, grocery chains, bars)
Brand positioning distinct from existing beer brands to avoid cannibalization
Sampling programs at events and festivals popular with millennials and Gen Z

recommendation: Big Beer Co should enter the alcoholic seltzer market via an Internal Launch.
The Internal Launch delivers the highest 5-year NPV of $1.75 billion, exceeds the $500M margin target, and stays within the 5-year payback requirement.
risks: Changing consumer tastes may erode the seltzer category before the 24-month internal launch is complete
New entrants may flood the market and compress margins
Inability to successfully launch the product in markets outside the US
Cannibalization of existing beer portfolio sales
Opportunity cost of capital and management attention diverted from core business
next_steps: Collaborate across R&D, manufacturing, and commercial teams to develop and launch the alcoholic seltzer product within 24 months
Conduct further analysis on other profitability initiatives identified in Question 5 (new categories, geographies, portfolio pruning)
